extra_context: We're a little independent toy shop tucked into a corner storefront, and we hand-pick everything ourselves — mostly wooden toys, open-ended building sets, weird wind-up critters, and games you won't find at the big-box stores. Our customers are parents and grandparents who want toys that aren't all plastic and batteries, plus the kids who light up the second they walk in. I want the shop to feel cozy and a bit magical, like a storybook you can wander into. The one thing everyone remembers is our "mystery cubby" wall up front — little numbered wooden boxes where for five bucks you get a surprise small toy, and kids beg to pick one every single visit.
